README: Hover help for every stimgen parameter and GUI control, in one place.
Read through stimgen.util.tooltip(source, key) -- see that function for the
lookup rules. JSON has no comments, hence this key; it is not a section.
Layout: one section per class, named without the package prefix. A lookup
searches the object's own section first, then each superclass section in
turn, so a subclass overrides an inherited entry simply by declaring the
same key (see ClickTrain.Duration). Keys must be valid MATLAB identifiers.
A property whose text depends on another property gets one key per case,
Keep each entry to a single line of plain text: what the parameter does,
plus any non-obvious consequence -- whether it is vectorizable, what a
value of 0 means, which other setting overrides it.

StimType.SoundLevel: Target level in dB SPL. Vectorizable for one variant per level. Requires loaded calibration.
StimType.ApplyCalibration: Scale to calibrated voltage. Off: normalized only, Sound Level is nominal.
StimType.Duration: Total waveform length in ms. Gate is applied inside this duration, not added to it.
StimType.WindowDuration: Onset + offset ramp length in ms (each ramp is half). Ignored when Apply Window is off.
StimType.ApplyWindow: Gate on/off to suppress spectral splatter from abrupt transitions.
StimType.VariantSelectionMode: Serial = table order; ShuffleUniform = random; ShuffleLeastUsed = random, least-presented first; CustomSelector = custom class.
StimType.VariantCombinationMode: Cartesian = all combinations; PairwiseStrict = element-wise, equal length; PairwiseScalarExpand = element-wise with scalar repeat.
StimType.VariantSelectorClass: Custom variant selector class name. Used only when Selection Mode is CustomSelector.
StimType.VariantReselectOnUpdate: Reselect variant every update. Off: variant fixed until manually stepped with < / >.

Tone.Frequency: Frequency in Hz. Vectorizable. Also used as the key for calibration lookup.
Tone.OnsetPhase: Starting phase in degrees. 0 = zero crossing, 90 = positive peak.
Tone.WindowMethod: Units for Window Duration: Duration (ms), Proportional (%), or #Periods (carrier periods). Changing this resets Window Duration.
Tone.WindowDuration_Proportional: Onset + offset ramp length as % of Duration. Each ramp is half. Ignored when Apply Window is off.
Tone.WindowDuration_Periods: Each onset and offset ramp in carrier periods, so ramp scales with Frequency. Ignored when Apply Window is off.

Noise.HighPass: Lower edge of the noise band in Hz. Must be below Low Pass Fc. Vectorizable.
Noise.LowPass: Upper edge of the noise band in Hz. Must be above High Pass Fc and below Fs/2. Vectorizable.

AMnoise.AMDepth: Depth 0–1. 0 = unmodulated, 1 = envelope to zero. Vectorizable.
AMnoise.OnsetPhase: Modulator phase in degrees. Default 180 starts at envelope minimum.
AMnoise.EnvelopeOnly: Output envelope only, without noise carrier. For checking envelope shape.
AMnoise.ApplyViemeisterCorrection: Normalize RMS power as Depth changes, keeping depth and level independent.

AttackModNoise.Z: Asymmetry: positive = damped (fast onset, slow decay), negative = ramped (slow onset, fast offset), 0 = symmetric. Magnitude controls sharpness.
AttackModNoise.AMDepth: Depth 0–1. Shape from Z; depth only feeds Viemeister correction.
AttackModNoise.AMRate: Envelope repetition rate in Hz. Vectorizable.
AttackModNoise.EnvelopeOnly: Output envelope only, without noise carrier. For checking envelope shape.
AttackModNoise.ApplyViemeisterCorrection: Normalize RMS power as Depth changes, keeping depth and level independent.

FMtone.ModulationFrequency: Sweep rate in Hz. 0 = unmodulated. Vectorizable.
FMtone.ModulationDepth: Peak deviation ±Hz from carrier. 0 = unmodulated. Vectorizable.

SweptSine.StartFrequency: Sweep start frequency in Hz. Must be < Stop Freq. Scalar only.
SweptSine.StopFrequency: Sweep end frequency in Hz. Must be > Start Freq and < Fs/2. Scalar only.
SweptSine.ChirpType: Log-sine: equal time per octave, pink spectrum (preferred calibration). Linear: constant Hz/s, emphasizes highs.

ClickTrain.Rate: Clicks per second. Interval 1/Rate must ≥ Click Duration. Vectorizable.
ClickTrain.ClickDuration: Click width in ms. Also calibration lookup key. Must be ≥1 sample at current Fs.
ClickTrain.Polarity: Alternate: flips each click, cancels stimulus artifact in averaged responses.
ClickTrain.OnsetDelay: Leading silence in ms. Train shifts within Duration, not added to it.
ClickTrain.Truncate: Cut at Duration instead of zero-padding. Train ends early if clicks don't fit a whole interval.
ClickTrain.Duration: Total train length in ms. Incomplete clicks are dropped; remainder zero-padded unless Truncate is on.

TORC.LowFrequency: Center frequency on tonotopic axis in Hz.
TORC.Bandwidth: Frequency range in octaves above LowFrequency.
TORC.ComponentMode: Range: single density scan. Explicit: custom rate/density pairs.
TORC.RippleDensity: Spectral density in cycles/octave. Sign sets spectral movement direction.
TORC.LowestRate: Lowest temporal modulation rate for Range mode.
TORC.HighestRate: Highest temporal modulation rate for Range mode.
TORC.ComponentRates: Space-separated temporal modulation rates for Explicit mode.
TORC.ComponentDensities: Space-separated ripple densities for Explicit mode. Recycled if shorter than rates.
TORC.RandomizeRipplePhase: Randomize ripple phases to reduce spectral peakiness.
TORC.Seed: Random seed for carrier and ripple phases. Negative reseeds randomly each update.
TORC.NumPeriods: Number of ripple periods in stimulus duration.

SoundFile.BrowseFiles: Add files to catalog. Files are added, not replaced. Each is one index entry.
SoundFile.UseAllFiles: Set File Index to every file, making one variant per file.
SoundFile.FileIndex: Which catalog entries to play by position. Vectorizable. Duration from selected file.
SoundFile.Channel: Channel to extract. 0 = mix all to mono.
SoundFile.CalibrationMode: Filtered = spectrum equalized (best broadband); Direct = no EQ, level at Anchor Freq (preserves shape); None = normalize only.
SoundFile.AnchorFrequency: Calibration reference for level in Direct mode. 0 = spectral centroid.
SoundFile.LevelReference: Statistic for Sound Level: rms (continuous), peak (transients).

StimPlayer.StimTypeDD: Stimulus class to create with Add Stim. Lists all classes in stimgen package.
StimPlayer.AddBtn: Add selected stimulus type to the bank.
StimPlayer.RemoveBtn: Delete selected stimulus from the bank.
StimPlayer.BankList: Bank stimuli. Select one to edit, preview, or step variants. Run presents all.
StimPlayer.BankLabel: Name shown in list and as workspace export field name.
StimPlayer.Reps: Presentations per run for selected item only. Other items keep their own count.
StimPlayer.ISI: Time between presentations in ms for whole bank. One value = fixed; [min max] = uniform range.
StimPlayer.SampleRate: Generation rate in Hz for all bank stimuli. Changing rebuilds all signals. Hardware rate overrides during protocol run.
StimPlayer.Order: Shuffle = random among items with reps left. Serial = down the list.
StimPlayer.ComboPrevBtn: Show previous variant combination (also left arrow key).
StimPlayer.ComboNextBtn: Show next variant combination (also right arrow key).
StimPlayer.ComboStatusLbl: Variant combination displayed / total for this stimulus.
StimPlayer.OutputDD: Speakers: normalized to unit peak (calibration levels not reproduced). Calibrated HW: verbatim waveform at calibrated level (needs host application).
StimPlayer.CalibrationStatusLabel: Green = calibrated levels played. Amber = calibration loaded but speaker preview normalizes. Red = no calibration.
StimPlayer.PlayBtn: Preview displayed combination. Does not advance run counter.
StimPlayer.PlayAllBtn: Preview all variant combinations in turn. Press again to stop.
StimPlayer.RunBtn: Start session: connect protocol, reset counters, present bank. Press again to stop.
StimPlayer.PauseBtn: Hold run without resetting. Press again to resume.
StimPlayer.ProtocolStatusLabel: Loaded protocol and hardware connection state. Falls back to speaker preview if protocol/params missing.
StimPlayer.ComputingLamp: On while generating stimulus signal. GUI briefly unresponsive.
StimPlayer.Counter: Stimuli presented / total for this run, summed over bank.

CalibrationGui.MaxOutputVoltage: Output ceiling in volts. Sets clipping limits on waveform display and marks unreachable voltages.
CalibrationGui.AdcGain: Input-stage gain of the rig, in dB. Recorded in the calibration file only -- nothing reads it back. The sweep was measured through this gain, so it is already inside every voltage and level in the tables; applying it again would double-count it. 0 dB = no gain.
CalibrationGui.DacAttenuation: Output-stage attenuation of the rig, in dB. Recorded in the calibration file only, on the same terms as ADC Gain: never applied to a level or a voltage. It is here so the file states the knob positions it was made at. 0 dB = no attenuation.
CalibrationGui.ConductionDelay: Speaker-to-microphone round-trip latency per acquisition, measured from embedded click. Includes converter latency. Red = unreliable (cross-correlation fallback). Distance is delay at speed of sound for Ambient Temperature.
CalibrationGui.AmbientTemperature: Air temperature (°F) for speed-of-sound calculations in impulse response distances. ±10° gives ~1% error. Saved in Celsius. Affects only distance display, not measured levels.
CalibrationGui.DelayMaxDelay: Max search range in ms for conduction delay probe. Raise if rig delay exceeds this (correlation peaks on bound, marked unreliable). 50 ms covers typical path + latency.
CalibrationGui.DelayNumClicks: Probe clicks. More = better SNR in noisy rooms, but risks aliasing if delay ~ click spacing. Default 1.
CalibrationGui.AcCoupleResponse: High-pass each record before analysis. Blocks DC offset and drift that corrupt RMS and leak into spectrum. Forward-backward (zero phase shift). Applies to next measurement only.
CalibrationGui.AcCoupleFrequency: AC-coupling corner in Hz. Set well below lowest calibrated frequency (already −3 dB at corner). 20 Hz typical; raise for mains hum.
CalibrationGui.ToneRampDuration: Per-edge rise/fall time for every tone burst played by Calibrate Tones, Test Tones, and refinement. Raised-cosine (cos^2) shape; clamped to a quarter of burst duration so onset/offset ramps never overlap. Longer suppresses click transients at burst edges; shorter leaves more steady-state signal on short bursts. Default 5 ms matches the fixed edge used before this was settable. Applies to the next tone measurement, and travels with the .esgc.
CalibrationGui.SpectralWindow: Auto: optimal window per use (flatTop for level, Hann for floor). Or choose fixed: flatTop accurate (~0.01 dB), Hann/Hamming/Blackman less leakage, Rectangular sharp but worst leakage. Applies to next measurement.
CalibrationGui.SpectralFftLength: Transform size. Auto: next power of 2 ≥record length. Manual only zero-pads (finer bins, better peak placement) never truncates. Costs time/memory on long records.
CalibrationGui.SettingsClose: Close this window. Nothing here waits to be confirmed -- every setting is applied to the calibration engine as soon as it is entered, so it takes effect whether or not this window is open.
CalibrationGui.ShowLivePlots: Update panels per measurement instead of only at end.
CalibrationGui.SpectrumUnits: dB SPL (calibration scale), V rms / dB re 1 V (mic input stage), density (per-Hz noise floor), or dB re peak (shape only). Applies immediately.
CalibrationGui.PrintSummary: Print a description of this calibration to the command window: the settings it was measured through, what each table covers, how each verification came out, and the notes. Same as Engine.describe at the prompt. Text, so it can be copied into a notebook entry.
CalibrationGui.CopyWindowTool: Copy the entire window (controls and plots) to the clipboard as an image. File > Save Screenshot... writes the same capture to a file.
CalibrationGui.QuickStartTool: Open calibration walkthrough on stimgen wiki.
CalibrationGui.GuiGuideTool: Open the guide to this window on the stimgen wiki: what each control does, in the order a calibration session uses them.
CalibrationGui.TabTones: Tone lookup table against frequency, with drive voltage per point, and the distortion and SNR measured at each frequency below it. Fills in live during a tone sweep or a tone LUT test.
CalibrationGui.TabClicks: Click lookup table against duration, with drive voltage per point, and the distortion and SNR measured at each duration below it. Fills in live during a click sweep or a click LUT test.
CalibrationGui.TabSweptSine: Swept sine lookup table, with the deconvolved response below it: magnitude flatness and group delay against frequency, and the impulse response with its arrival and first reflection.
CalibrationGui.TabFilterTest: Equalization filter verification: the response with and without the filter in dB SPL, and below it each one's deviation from flat against the ripple tolerance. Fills in live during Test Filter; the comparison is drawn when the run ends.
CalibrationGui.TabBackground: Background noise: band levels, broadband/A-weighted level, tonal peaks. Drawn by Measure Background.
CalibrationGui.TabLatency: Conduction delay probe: the click correlation the delay was chosen from, over the probe response. Drawn by Measure Conduction Delay.
CalibrationGui.SpectrumGhost: Overlay previous measurement in grey. Shows run-to-run drift and flaky connections.
CalibrationGui.TransferVoltage: Show drive voltage per calibrated point and output ceiling. Points above ceiling unreachable at target level.
CalibrationGui.TransferLogX: Log frequency axis (audio standard) vs linear (click duration view).
CalibrationGui.FullResolutionWaveforms: Draw every sample of the response, excitation and probe records instead of the min/max envelope. Slower to redraw on long records; the envelope keeps every block's peak, so clipping and transients show either way. Turn on when zoomed in far enough to want the shape within a block.
CalibrationGui.BtnReference: Step 1: Record acoustic calibrator (e.g. PCB CAL150) on microphone. Updates mic sensitivity. Records only.
CalibrationGui.BtnBackground: Optional after Measure Reference: record and analyze ambient noise. Records only (remove calibrator). Broadband/A-weighted/octave bands + tonal peaks.
CalibrationGui.BtnTones: Step 2: Frequency sweep to build tone calibration table.
CalibrationGui.BtnSweptSine: Optional: Broadband chirp calibration. Can also serve tone lookups (Tone Lookup From Swept Sine).
CalibrationGui.ToneLutFromSweptSine: Use swept-sine table for tone lookups instead of direct tone table while checked. Both stay stored. Choice saved in .esgc.
CalibrationGui.IterativeRefinement: Test each point at its table voltage, correct errors, repeat until target accuracy or pass limit. Removes nonlinear gain not scaled as 20*log10(voltage).
CalibrationGui.BtnTestTones: Step 3: Verify tone table. Play at table voltages, compare returned vs requested levels. Tests midway between calibrated frequencies (interpolation test).
CalibrationGui.BtnTestClicks: Verify click table. Play at table voltages, compare returned vs requested peak levels. Tests midway between calibrated durations.
CalibrationGui.BtnFilter: Step 4 (optional): Design equalization filter. Opens in fvtool.
CalibrationGui.BtnTestFilter: Step 5 (optional): Empirically verify designed filter. Tone design tested with discrete tones; swept sine tested with sweep + filtered sweep.
CalibrationGui.BtnCopyFilter: Copy FIR coefficients to clipboard (one per line, full precision) for RPvds, spreadsheet, or other use. Realization rate in status bar.
CalibrationGui.FilterLevelReference: Output level for 1 V RMS white-noise input at unity gain after filter. Scale factor (x) for Normative Value. Hardware gain = 10^((level−Normative Value)/20) × scale. Recomputed per filter design. Anchor hardware to scale OR to this level, never both — the two are one correction.
CalibrationGui.BtnDelay: Measure conduction delay standalone via embedded click. Reports air path at 343 m/s. No reference or calibration table needed. Not consumed by subsequent measurements.
CalibrationGui.BtnStop: Interrupt running measurement (takes effect at next acquisition). Discards partial data. Refinement restores unrefined table.
CalibrationGui.BtnReset: Discard all tone/click/swept-sine data and designed filter. Keeps adapter, protocol, mic sensitivity, other settings.
CalibrationGui.Notes: Free text about this calibration: speaker, microphone, placement, anything the tables cannot say for themselves. Saved into the .esgc and restored with it, and printed by File > Print Calibration Summary. Not a preference -- it belongs to this calibration, not to the rig, and a reset leaves it alone.

StimInspector.ExportTool: Export signal and metrics to workspace

SpotCheck.LoadBtn: Load a stimulus to check, from a .spl bank or a .mat holding a StimType.
SpotCheck.MatchRateBtn: Set the stimulus sample rate to the hardware's. Regenerates the waveform.
SpotCheck.RunBtn: Play the stimulus, record the microphone, and compare. Cancels a run in progress.
SpotCheck.PreDelay: Silence before the stimulus, in ms. The noise floor is measured over it.
SpotCheck.PostDelay: Silence after the stimulus, in ms. Must exceed the rig round-trip latency or the response cannot be located.
SpotCheck.Repeats: Acquisitions to average. Each is aligned on its own delay first.
SpotCheck.InspectCaptureTool: Open a Stimulus Inspector on the recording
SpotCheck.InspectStimTool: Open a Stimulus Inspector on the stimulus
SpotCheck.SaveTool: Save the spot check, both waveforms and all metrics, to a .mat
SpotCheck.ShotTool: Save the whole window, plots and table, to an image file
SpotCheck.SummaryTool: Print the spot check to the command window

CapturedSignal.SourceLabel: What was played to produce this record. Free text, carried with the samples.
CapturedSignal.Waveform: The captured samples, in volts. Reported exactly as recorded: never normalized, gated or scaled.
